rules.text: Japanese Knotweed Not Inspected: Japanese Knotweed: Dense vegetation or restricted access prevented a full inspection of the grounds. Consequently, I cannot confirm whether Japanese knotweed or other invasive plants are present. Further investigation by a suitably qualified specialist is recommended if required.

Not Found: No evidence of Japanese knotweed was observed within the areas inspected. However, the inspection was limited to those areas that were visible and reasonably accessible at the time of the survey, and its absence cannot be guaranteed. Recent gardening works, dense vegetation, or other ground cover may conceal evidence of invasive plants and prevent their identification during a visual inspection.

Found: Japanese knotweed was identified within or adjacent to the property boundary. This invasive plant can damage hard landscaping and, in some circumstances, affect structures. It may also affect mortgageability, insurability, marketability, and value. I recommend that you arrange for further inspection by a remediation specialist who is a member of a recognised body so that you can get advice about future management and control and an insurance-backed guarantee.

Management A: Japanese knotweed is present and has caused damage to building structures and/or boundary features. A suitably qualified invasive weed specialist should inspect the site without delay and implement an appropriate treatment and remediation programme.
Management B: Japanese knotweed is present and is adversely affecting the use of the property or its amenities. A specialist treatment and management plan should be implemented.

Management C: Japanese knotweed is present, but no damage to buildings or boundary structures was evident at the time of inspection. A specialist management or treatment programme is nevertheless recommended.

Management D: Japanese knotweed was observed on neighbouring land within approximately three metres of the property boundary. Although no damage was evident to the subject property, the infestation should be monitored, and your legal adviser should make appropriate enquiries where necessary.
